text.p: Ethiopia's parliament on Thursday approved a 10.452 billion birr ($1.6 billion) budget for 1997/98 and said its priority was to reduce poverty.
State-radio said the budget was referred to a committee for scrutiny on Friday after Prime Minister Meles Zenawi presented it to parliament. It was approved unanimously.
Ethiopia's expenditure in 1996/97 (July/June) was posted at 9.75 billion birr.
Meles said that of the 10.452 billion, about 6.8 billion was federal expenditure while the balance would subsidise regional governments.
Meles said the government's main focus in the financial year 1997/98 would be on 249 projects in the energy, education, construction and telecommunications sectors.
Meles said the government will not borrow from banks and would also not sell securities in the market to raise resources to cover recurrent expenditure.
"This year's budget is a zero budget as it relates to local resources, the ministry of finance will not sell securities to raise money," Meles said.
"But, we still have deficit in the capital budget outlay which will be covered through grants, assistance and commerical loans from abroad," he added.
Meles told parliament that Ethiopia's economy in the 1996/97 period grew by 7.0 percent and the rate of inflation eased to negative 6.9 percent.
GDP growth for 1997/78 was projected at between nine and 10 percent. GDP growth reached 7.7 percent in 1995.
Meles said the volume of Ethiopia's export trade -- the bulk of which is coffee -- grew by 16 percent while import trade increased by 30 percent during the period 1996/97.
Ethiopia exported a record 119,804 tonnes of coffee and earned $352.5 million in the first ten months of 1996/97, according to the country's coffee officials.
Final figures for the crop (July/June) are expected later this month, according to finance ministry sources. ($ = 6.596 Ethiopian Birr)
